# Results — Study 849 (Dry January / Veganuary)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the two
January cultural waves, **Dry January** (abstain from alcohol) and **Veganuary** (go
plant-based), shift consumer demand hard and predictably enough to move the relevant stocks
in January: alcohol names (`BUD, STZ, TAP, DEO, SAM`) should *under*-perform, plant-based
`BYND` should *out*-perform, staples `XLP` is a flat control — all measured as an **abnormal**
return vs `SPY`. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Fingerprint `e5210651db30` (the eight-ticker daily close panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return, `auto_adjust=True`) closes, **8 tickers** (`BUD STZ TAP DEO SAM BYND XLP SPY`), one combined panel: **6,914** rows, 1999-01-04 → 2026-06-30 |
| Groups | **alcohol** = equal-weight `BUD, STZ, TAP, DEO, SAM` (Dry-January names) · **plant** = `BYND` (Veganuary name, inception mid-2019) · **staples** = `XLP` (boring control) · **bench** = `SPY` |
| Unit of test | one **month-end simple return** per name per month; the abnormal return of a group is `group − SPY`; the January seasonal is read across the **independent yearly Januaries** (the correct unit — one observation per year, not a daily panel) |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the January (and February) abnormal return; a **Newey-West** (HAC, Bartlett, 3-lag) *t* on the coefficient of a January dummy in a monthly regression; a Wilson hit-rate; a 12-month calendar placebo; a two-era robustness cut; a costed once-a-year timer; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known, zero look-ahead** — January is always January. The timer enters at the December month-end close and exits at the January month-end close, net of 2× one-way cost × NAV on each of two legs plus one month of borrow on the short alcohol leg |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested) for every leg |

**Zero look-ahead by construction.** The calendar is fixed and known decades ahead, so a
"is January's abnormal return different from the other eleven months?" test carries no
survivorship or peeking. A semi-strong-efficient market prices a calendar everyone can read;
the desk's prior is nothing. **Two small-n caveats, named:** `BYND` supplies only **7**
Januaries (listed 2019), so the whole plant / plant-minus-alcohol side is a thin-sample
curiosity; and `XLP` is a low-beta staple, which is why we quote the *abnormal* return
throughout, never the raw move.

## The headline — January abnormal return (group − SPY), one observation per year

| group | n (Jan) | mean AR | one-sample *t* | NW *t* (dummy) | hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **alcohol** (Dry-January names) | 27 | **−1.20%** | **−1.28** | −1.46 | 10/27 = 37.0% |
| **plant** `BYND` (Veganuary) | 7 | +12.71% | +1.23 | +1.82 | 5/7 |
| **staples** `XLP` (control) | 27 | −0.62% | −0.80 | −0.59 | 13/27 |
| **plant − alcohol** (pure thesis) | 7 | +14.46% | +1.33 | +1.76 | 5/7 |

The folklore points **exactly the right way — but never clears the bar.** In January the
alcohol basket is the *weakest*, plant-based `BYND` the *strongest*, and the market-neutral
plant-minus-alcohol spread is firmly positive — the precise fingerprint Dry-January /
Veganuary would leave. Yet the alcohol drag (the one leg with a real sample, 27 Januaries)
is only −1.20% at *t* = −1.28 (NW *t* = −1.46), and the eye-catching +14.5% plant-minus-alcohol
spread rests on **7 years** of a famously volatile single stock (*t* = +1.33). Nothing reaches
|*t*| ≥ 2. The staples control is a flat −0.62% (*t* = −0.80), as it should be.

## February "hangover"

| group | n (Feb) | mean AR | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| alcohol | 28 | +0.12% | +0.13 |
| plant `BYND` | 7 | +2.30% | +0.20 |
| staples `XLP` | 28 | +0.58% | +0.77 |

The predicted February *bounce* in the alcohol names (abstainers fall off the wagon) is
essentially **zero** (+0.12%, *t* = +0.13). There is no hangover trade.

## Calendar placebo — is January special, or one of twelve months?

Rank January's mean abnormal return among all twelve calendar months (directional tail):

| group | tail (claim) | Jan mean | rank | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| alcohol | left (Dry-January drag) | −1.20% | **1 / 12** | 0.083 |
| plant `BYND` | right (Veganuary lift) | +12.71% | **1 / 12** | 0.083 |
| plant − alcohol | right | +14.46% | **1 / 12** | 0.083 |

All three land January at **rank 1 of 12** in the folklore's predicted direction — alcohol is
the single most-negative month, plant the single most-positive. That directional agreement is
the strongest thing in the study; but the pre-specified-month placebo can do no better than
p = 1/12 ≈ 0.083, which does not clear 0.05, and it rides on the same thin samples.

## Robustness — alcohol January abnormal return, two eras (split 2013)

| era | n | mean AR | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1999-2012 | 13 | −1.58% | −1.37 |
| 2013-2026 | 14 | −0.85% | −0.57 |

The alcohol January drag is the **right sign in both halves**, but it fades to a *t* of −0.57
in the modern era — sign-consistent, magnitude-shrinking, never significant.

## The timer — long-plant / short-alcohol every January, costed

Enter at the December close, hold the plant-minus-alcohol book through January, exit at the
January close (calendar-known). Charge 2× one-way × NAV on each of two legs + one month borrow.

| one-way cost | n years | gross | cost | net | *t* (net) | hit |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **5 bps** | 7 | +14.46% | 0.24% | **+14.22%** | +1.31 | 5/7 |
| **10 bps** | 7 | +14.46% | 0.44% | **+14.02%** | +1.29 | 5/7 |

The trade *survives costs* only because friction is trivial next to `BYND`'s wild moves — but
it is **7 observations at *t* = +1.31**, a capacity-trivial once-a-year bet dominated by a
single small-cap's early tape. Not significant, not scalable: a **Mirage**.

## Synthetic positive control — the detector is unbiased

Deterministic seeded (NAME, SPY) tape with a *tunable* planted January abnormal-return
seasonal (`edge`). No network. Averaged over **20 seeds** (house rule):

| world | mean NW *t* | mean beta | \|*t*\| ≥ 2 fires |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`) | **−0.20** | −0.26% | **0 / 20 (0%)** |
| planted (`edge = 0.02`) | +1.39 | +1.76% | 20% |
| planted (`edge = 0.05`) | **+3.77** | +4.85% | 90% |

The detector never fires on the null and recovers a planted January seasonal monotonically
(a genuine +5% January edge would light up 90% of the time) — so the sub-threshold real-tape
result is a true *absence of a strong effect*, not a power failure. *(A faithful-engine check
only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the January demand shift real?** | **Weak** | The folklore's fingerprint is **directionally perfect**: the alcohol basket is the *most-negative* calendar month (−1.20%, rank 1/12) and `BYND` the *most-positive* (rank 1/12), sign-consistent across both eras. But the only well-sampled leg (alcohol, 27 Januaries) reaches just *t* = −1.28 (NW −1.46), the plant / spread side rides on **7** noisy `BYND` years (*t* ≈ +1.3), the February hangover is absent, and **no cut clears |*t*| ≥ 2**. The 20-seed control shows the detector *would* fire on a genuine +5% seasonal (90%), so this is a real-but-sub-threshold whiff — a directional hint, not an established effect. |
| **Tradability — can you get paid?** | **Mirage** | The long-plant / short-alcohol January timer nets **+14.2%/yr** at 5 bps — but on **7 observations at *t* = +1.31**, driven by one small-cap's early tape, once a year, capacity-trivial and inside a multi-cut search. Nothing bankable. |

**In one sentence:** Dry January and Veganuary leave *exactly the right footprint* in the tape
— alcohol is the year's weakest month and plant-based its strongest — but at *t* ≈ −1.3 / +1.2
on 27 and just 7 Januaries the seasonal never clears the significance bar, so it is a charming
directional hint with no tradable paycheck.
